# S3 Glacier Archive Server

> Go application that stores timestamped objects in local TAR archives, with HTTP,
> a subset of S3, and a web interface. Module path: glacier. This is not a client
> for the AWS S3 Glacier storage service.

## Documentation

- [README](README.md): startup, storage layout, supported features, and limitations.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): environment-only settings and defaults.
- [HTTP and S3 API](docs/api.md): routes, authentication, examples, and errors.
- [OpenAPI](docs/openapi.yaml): JSON bucket management API only.
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): build, testing, lint, and documentation checks.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): user-visible development changes.
- [License](LICENSE): Apache License 2.0.

## Implementation

- [main.go](main.go): server construction and route registration; web assets are embedded.
- [bucket](bucket/store.go): immutable bucket definitions and creation.
- [shared](shared/shared.go): UUID resolution, archive placement, and object I/O.
- [archive](archive/store.go): process-local archive locks, durable checkpoints,
  immutable object retries, recovery, and coordinated eviction.
- [s3](s3/s3.go): S3 credential registry and V2/V4 authentication dispatch.
- [autoclean](autoclean/autoclean.go): global disk-pressure archive removal.
- [config](config/settings.go): environment settings; startup logs include their values.

## Contracts

Every bucket has a fixed maximum TAR count per hour, from 1 to 65,536. The default
bucket data uses 256. Persist all of DATA_FOLDER, including .buckets metadata and
each TAR's .commit checkpoint. One serving process per data root is required;
in-memory locks are keyed by full bucket/hour/shard and do not cross hours. One
lifetime .server.lock enforces standalone-server ownership; use a local filesystem
with file/directory sync, atomic rename, and power-safe overwrite semantics.
An object name must contain a supported lowercase UUID v1 or timestamped UUID v4.
Uploads buffer a complete object in memory. Identical UUID/content retries are
idempotent; conflicting bytes return 409. Successful uploads sync the TAR and
checkpoint before acknowledgment. Recovery hides uncommitted tails; archives
without the checkpoint/manifest format are not automatically migrated.
Per-object overwrite/delete, S3 object listing,
and S3 multipart upload are unsupported. HTTP multipart upload is supported.
HTTP tokens and S3 signing credentials are separate and server-wide.

## Development

Use the Go version in go.mod. Run make test and make lint; use
`go test -tags=integration -race -shuffle=on -count=1 -timeout=5m ./...` for race and crash-recovery checks.
`make modernize` edits code through go fix and requires diff review afterward.
